subjective: Max has shown sudden aggression towards another dog since yesterday, including bouncing on and trying to fight. He has been tense, not strong, and walking away at times. Max is friendly with the owner but has not been eating properly since yesterday, including refusing his favorite food. There is a history of occasional aggression between the two dogs, possibly triggered by the female dog showing teeth or food-related issues. The female dog tries to engage Max in play, but he is unresponsive. Attempts to separate feeding areas have been made to prevent fights. Max’s appetite remains poor, and he did not eat during a recent walk when the female dog tried to eat his food.
objective: Max is tense and shows behavioral changes consistent with aggression and decreased appetite. Temperature is somewhat elevated (exact value not provided). No direct physical examination findings or diagnostic test results are documented in the conversation. No medication currently administered.
assessment: Max is exhibiting behavioral aggression possibly related to inter-dog dynamics, hormonal influences, or food-related triggers. The decreased appetite and mild fever may be associated with a vaccine reaction or an underlying illness. Further diagnostic testing is recommended to determine the cause of the fever and behavioral changes.
plan: Recommend a 10-day vaccination shot as planned. Advise laboratory testing to identify the cause of the elevated temperature. No medication is currently needed for vaccine-related fever as it should resolve spontaneously. Owner instructed to discourage the female dog's food-seeking behavior by withholding food rewards to reduce aggression. Continue to separate feeding areas to prevent fights. Monitor Max’s appetite and behavior closely. Provide documentation after annual vaccination. Follow-up as needed based on test results and clinical progression.
conclusion: Max presented with sudden aggression towards another dog and decreased appetite since yesterday. Behavioral changes include tension and avoidance. The female dog’s behavior may be contributing to the aggression. Max has a mildly elevated temperature, possibly due to vaccine reaction or other causes. Laboratory testing is advised to determine the origin of the fever. No medication is currently required. Owner advised on behavioral management and feeding separation. Vaccination will proceed with documentation provided. Close monitoring and follow-up are recommended.
key_issues: 1. Aggression between Max and the female dog, possibly triggered by hormonal influences or food-related conflicts. 2. Decreased appetite and mild fever, possibly related to vaccine reaction or underlying illness.
abnormal_findings: Elevated temperature (fever) noted. Behavioral aggression and decreased appetite.
customer_instructions: Separate feeding areas to prevent fights. Do not give food or rewards to the female dog after feeding to discourage aggressive or food-seeking behavior. Monitor Max’s appetite and behavior. Proceed with vaccination and laboratory testing as advised. No medication needed for vaccine-related fever unless symptoms worsen.
reminders: Follow-up after laboratory test results. Monitor for changes in behavior or appetite. Provide documentation after annual vaccination.
